Force-encode a scalar string for the DataSHIELD expression transport

Source: R/manipulate.R
dot-ds_encode_scalar.Rd

.ds_encode only base64-wraps lists and multi-element vectors; a scalar string passes through as a bare literal. That is a problem for the filter operator: the comparison operators (">=", ">", "==", ...) contain <, >, = characters that the DataSHIELD expression lexer (DSLite and Opal) refuses inside a bare string literal ("Syntax error"). Wrapping the value as a single-element list routes it through the same URL-safe base64 path, and the server-side .ds_arg transparently decodes it back to the scalar.

Usage

.ds_encode_scalar(x)

Arguments

x

A length-1 character value.

Value

A B64:-prefixed token that the server's .ds_arg decodes back to the scalar string.
